title: The Siren Song of LLMs: How Users Perceive and Respond to Dark Patterns in Large Language Models
reasoning: The paper investigates 'dark patterns,' which are inherently defined as manipulative and deceptive interaction strategies. It conducts a user study evaluating how participants perceive these unethical behaviors. Additionally, one of the primary scenarios used to test user perception (Sycophantic Agreement) specifically utilizes 'spiritualized framing' and 'spiritual goals' as a vector for manipulation.
